Almost all of this folio is unreadable at the available resolution. The ink is very faint brown on blue-grey paper, and the machine transcription recovers essentially no text. I am therefore reporting what is visually recognisable on the page and offering a tentative, explicitly hypothetical interpretation. I am not claiming to reconstruct any derivation.

Visible structure:
(a) About 7 lines of German prose continue an argument from the previous page (13r).
(b) A short paragraph begins with something like 'Nun ...'.
(c) There is a centred short heading of about 2 words, then about 3 lines of prose.
(d) A centred section numeral, read as 'II.' or '11.'. The previous page also carries an '11.', so the sheets probably carry numbered sections.
(e) A long paragraph follows that contains inline formula fragments. One looks like an equation of the form 'f(ζ, ζ', ζ'') = 0' or 'ϑ(...) = 0'. Later in the paragraph appear fragments that look like subscripted variables, an expression set equal to 0, and possibly 'p' or 'ρ'.
(f) A paragraph of about 5 lines, then one of about 4 lines, ending with something like '... (= 0 für ... ?)'.
(g) The page closes with a short tabulated case list. Its left margin reads roughly 'für p = 1', and a later line is marked 'p ≥ 2' (or 'p > 2'). Each row seems to have three parts: a value or condition on p; an equation of the form 'ϑ(ζ/?, ζ/?) = 0' or 'Θ(...) = 0' with fractional arguments; and a value 'r = 0', 'r = 0', 'r = (p−1)...', 'r = (p−1)(p−2)...'.

Tentative interpretation (mine, not established): the symbols p, ϑ(...) = 0 with arguments that look like halves, and an integer r depending on p suggest Riemann's theory of Abelian/theta functions. Here p would be the genus. The vanishing of ϑ at half-period arguments would correspond to odd characteristics. r would be either the multiplicity or order of vanishing, or a count of solutions/conditions, tabulated for p = 1, p = 2 and general p. This would fit Riemann's work toward the 1857 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' or the 1865/66 theta-vanishing paper.

Alternative hypothesis: the bundle is labelled 1853, so the page could instead belong to an unrelated project of that period, such as a classification of surfaces or equations with case distinctions on a parameter p. That would be consistent with 'f(...) = 0' type equations and an index r.

At this resolution I cannot read the actual equations, the arguments of ϑ, or the formulas for r, so no step-by-step derivation can be honestly given.

checkable.asserts: Genus-1 case: the odd Jacobi theta function θ1 vanishes at argument 0, i.e. the theta function with odd half-integer characteristic vanishes at the origin (plausible content of the 'p = 1' row; r = 0 would correspond to a simple zero).
The odd and even theta characteristics in genus p together number 4^p (2^{p-1}(2^p-1) odd, 2^{p-1}(2^p+1) even); this standard count is a possible background for a case table in p.
